teaser.text: T-Mobile US sells access to communications networks, chiefly mobile phone service but also home and business internet. Its business is the conversion of network capacity, devices and customer relationships into recurring payments, with costs and investment determining what remains.

stock.meta_description: T-Mobile stock forecast weighs three scenarios against customer retention, cash delivery, execution and valuation.
stock.opening: T-Mobile’s weighted forecast reaches $278.03 in October 2029. It hinges on whether T-Mobile converts acquired customer growth and network investment into durable cash without weakening service.
stock.closing: The full memo explains T-Mobile’s business, rivals, management choices and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could T-Mobile’s shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted path starts at $153.43 today and reaches $201.09 in October 2027. That first leg represents a +34% return. The final weighted price is $278.03 in October 2029, a +91% return. Bear probability is 25%; base probability is 55%. Bull probability is 20%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for T-Mobile?

paragraphs.text: The bear case begins at $157.82 in October 2027 and ends at $161.92 in October 2029, including dividends, with a 25% probability. Plan changes raise churn, account growth weakens and capacity or satellite competition forces more promotions. EBITDA falls, the multiple compresses to 6x and lower cash generation limits buybacks. The probability remains below the base because EBITDA has risen every year in the recent record.

The base case has a 55% probability. It assumes the 2026–27 plans broadly hold, integration and digitalization improve operating leverage, and buybacks continue within cash generation. The multiple stays at 7.5x, producing $204.42 first and $279.06 by the final date.

The bull case rises from $246.03 to $420.31 and carries a 20% probability. Retention holds, premium plans lift account economics, digital savings exceed transition costs and broadband grows without disproportionate investment. Stronger cash then funds larger buybacks and supports multiple expansion. Several conditions must succeed together, which limits its odds.

blocks.heading: How much cash does T-Mobile really make?

paragraphs.text: In 2025, operating cash flow was $27,950 million. After broader capital spending of $12,523 million, free cash flow was $15,427 million. Subtracting $829 million of stock compensation gives an economic “real” free cash flow of $14,598 million, recognising that employees received part of their compensation through shareholders’ ownership.

dividend.title: T-Mobile dividend: cash coverage and yield
dividend.meta_description: T-Mobile's dividend is supported by real free cash flow, with its yield shown against the share price and risks to future payouts.
dividend.opening: T-Mobile pays a declared $1.17 quarterly dividend. The memo says T-Mobile's real free cash flow covers the dividend, while dividends and buybacks take most free cash flow.
dividend.closing: The full memo also examines T-Mobile's business, rivals, management, and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does T-Mobile pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Dividends start from the declared $1.17 quarterly rate. Base DPS rises from $4.68 to $5.38 and then $6.19, using the latest 15% increase as a scenario pace. The bear falls to $4.08 and then $3.67 as cash pressure emerges; the bull reaches $5.38 immediately and compounds to $7.12. Recent cash generation supports increases, but distributions already consumed almost all first-half free cash flow.

blocks.heading: Is T-Mobile's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Dividends send cash directly to shareholders, while buybacks retire shares so each remaining share represents more of the company. T-Mobile paid out most of its free cash flow through both channels, especially by 2025. That can support per-share earnings, but it does not itself improve the network. The decision creates value only if the shares are bought at sensible prices and the financing remains manageable.

earnings.title: T-Mobile earnings: date, guidance and results
earnings.meta_description: T-Mobile's next results are expected October 28, 2026, with guidance on customers, cash flow and service revenue, plus key risks to watch.
earnings.opening: T-Mobile's next results are expected on October 28, 2026. For T-Mobile, the key thing to watch is whether higher bills lift account revenue without driving away enough households.
earnings.closing: The full memo explains T-Mobile's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: What has T-Mobile guided for 2026 and 2027?

paragraphs.text: Management expects 950,000–1,050,000 net account additions in 2026 and ARPA growth of 2.5%–3.0%. Its 2026 plan pairs that customer growth with service revenue of US$77,000 million, Core Adjusted EBITDA of US$37,100–37,500 million and adjusted free cash flow of US$18,400–18,800 million after US$10,000 million of cash capital expenditure.

The 2027 plan raises service revenue to US$80,500–81,500 million and assigns US$3,000 million of EBITDA contribution to digitalization and AI, including more self-service through T-Life. But the latest cash-flow increase came mainly from lower cash taxes. Q1 and Q2 produced 494,000 net account additions, leaving 456,000–556,000 for the second half while plan changes were expected to raise churn temporarily.

blocks.heading: Has T-Mobile kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Promises provide a final performance test. A 2021 plan projected service revenue above US$70 billion by 2026. Revenue reached US$71.3 billion in 2025, though acquisitions affect comparability. The same presentation described potential shareholder returns up to US$60 billion during 2023–2025. Reported cumulative returns were US$45.4 billion through 2025, including activity before 2023.

blocks.heading: How have T-Mobile's revenue and profit trended?

paragraphs.text: The June 2026 quarter showed resilient operations, but not uniformly stronger growth. Revenue reached $22,791 million, up 7.9%, while operating income rose 5.3% to $5,490 million. Net income rose only 0.5%, although diluted EPS increased 5.3% as the share count fell.

blocks.heading: What should T-Mobile watchers look for next?

paragraphs.text: The next scheduled earnings call is October 28, 2026, at 4:30 p.m. Eastern. Management expected approximately 250,000 net account additions in Q3 despite temporarily higher departures after its rate-plan modernization. The test is whether higher bills lift account revenue without driving away enough households to damage the recurring relationship.
